name: Pearls and Jade Pothos
description: A patented sport of Marble Queen developed at the University of Florida, Pearls and Jade is a compact, small-leaved pothos with a distinctive variegation pattern: green centers surrounded by irregular margins of white and grey-green, often with fine speckling and patches that push in from the leaf edges rather than streaking through the middle. The leaves are smaller than most pothos (2-4 inches), and the plant stays notably compact and slow-growing, making it ideal for small pots, shelves, and tight spaces. Because the variegation includes a lot of white and grey, it needs bright indirect light to look its best and grows more slowly than green pothos. Otherwise it shares the same forgiving, near-indestructible pothos temperament that makes the whole family so beginner-friendly.
toxicity: Toxic to cats, dogs and horses. Chewing it causes mouth pain and swelling, drooling, vomiting and difficulty swallowing.

symptoms: Pain and swelling of the mouth, tongue and lips

careInstructions: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil are dry - typically weekly, and slightly less as it grows slowly
Provide medium to bright indirect light to keep variegation crisp
Avoid harsh direct sun, which scorches the white margins
Prune to maintain its compact shape and encourage fullness
Propagates easily from stem cuttings below a node
Wipe the small leaves gently to keep them clean
Fertilize every other month during spring and summer with diluted balanced fertilizer - skip winter
Expect slow, compact growth - normal for this cultivar
commonProblems: Loss of variegation / reverting to green: Insufficient light - move to a brighter spot
Brown speckles or crispy white margins: Sunburn from direct light or low humidity
Yellow leaves: Usually overwatering - allow soil to dry more between waterings
Brown leaf tips: Fluoride or chlorine sensitivity - use filtered water
Very slow growth: Normal for this compact cultivar, or needs brighter light
Root rot: Overwatering or poor drainage

fertilizing.tip: Fertilize every other month during spring and summer with diluted balanced fertilizer - skip winter

whatsNormal: Variegated pothos grow more slowly than all-green ones and need brighter light to keep their color — in low light the pale patches shrink.
Older leaves yellow and drop over time, so leaves bunch toward the ends of the vines — prune stems back to keep it full.

propagation.tip: Cut below a node and root it in water or moist mix.

flags.note: Sources cover Epipremnum aureum, not the 'Pearls and Jade' cultivar. The brighter light for variegation follows NC State and Clemson's notes on variegated pothos.
Winter watering interval (10 days) is our estimate — the sources only say to reduce watering from fall to late winter.
Fertilizing monthly → every other month, matching the Pothos research (NC State, Wisconsin).
